(Aqueous tension at $300 \mathrm{~K}=15 \mathrm{~mm}$ )

$\begin{aligned} & \frac{p_1 V_1}{T_1}=\frac{p_2 V_2}{T_2} \\ & \text{$ or $} \frac{\left(\rho-\rho_1\right)}{T_1} V_1=\frac{p_2 V_2}{T_2}\end{aligned}$
where,
$p_1=\rho-\rho_1\rho=715 \mathrm{~mm}$ (pressure at which $\mathrm{N}_2$ collected).
$\begin{aligned} & \rho_1=\text{ aqueous tension$ of $water }=15 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & t_1=t+273=300 \mathrm{~K} \\ & V_1=55 \mathrm{~mL}=\text{ Volume of moist nitrogen in } \\ & \text{ nitrometer } \\ & \rho_2=\text{ pressure of } \mathrm{N}_2 \text{ at } \mathrm{STP}=760 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & t_2=\text{ temperature of } \mathrm{N}_2 \text{ at } \mathrm{STP}=273 \mathrm{~K} \\ & V_2=\text{ ? }\end{aligned} \therefore V_2=\frac{(715-15)}{300} \times 55 \times \frac{273}{760}=46.098 \mathrm{~mL} \%$ of nitrogen in the given compound

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which amongst the following is the most stable carbocation?
questions.solution:
The most stable carbocation is $t$-alkyl carbocation because the order of stability of alkyl carbocation is $t$-alkyl $\gt s$-alkyl $\gt$ p-alkyl $\gt \mathrm{CH}_3^{+}$ carbocation. This stability order is described with the help of hyperconjugation and inductive effect. On the basis of hyper conjugation, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}$ shows six resonating structures due to presence of six $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds,

due to presence of nine $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds $\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3$ does not show the property of resonance while $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2$ shows three resonating structures due to presence of three $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds. Hence, larger number of resonating structures are possible in (2), so it is most stable. The above order of stability is also explained with the help of (+) I-effect of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. More the number of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. more will be tendency to displace the electrons towards positive charged carbon of carbocation. Thus (+) charge is decreased or compensated i.e, positive charge is decreased and stability of carbocation is increased.

questions.solution: Aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$ is used to separate benzoic acid from its mixture with camphor. Benzoic acid form water soluble sodium benzoate with $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Dihedral angle between two methyl groups of $n$-butane in the gauche and anti forms are
questions.solution: (The angle between $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds on adjacent carbon atoms in any conformation is called dihedral angle.) Hence, the dihedral angle in case of gauche is $60^{\circ}$ and in anti form is $180^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which carbocation is most stable?
questions.solution: A phenyl group, in which there is a flow of electron due to resonance of the benzene ring, generally causes -I effect, but truely speaking it can act as both electron donating as well as electron withdrawing groups, depending upon the nature of group with which it is attached. In $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2^{+}$, phenyl group is attached to electron deficient group, hence it will donate electron due to resonance in benzene ring and thus stabilise the cation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of stability of carbocations, is :
questions.solution:
More the +I alkyl groups on electron deficient carbon, more stable will be the cabocation. Hence, $3^{\circ}$ carbocations are more stable.
The correct order is $3^{\circ}\gt2^{\circ}\gt1^{\circ}\gt\mathrm{CH}_3^+$
